Venice's private-mode / model-picker / image-gen surfaces may exist but are NOT catalogued — do not assume; re-verify on first live capture. GOAL 160: `answer` was the bare class-substring selector `[class*="message"]`, which matches the ASSISTANT MESSAGE CONTAINER — and that container also holds the model's reasoning/preamble block. The readback takes the LONGEST matching element, so when the reasoning block is longer than the eventual answer it is what gets served: MEASURED 2026-09-30, HTTP 200 with `The user wants me to reply with exactly "PONG". This` after 41611ms. That is a SELECTOR-PRECISION defect (the selector is not scoped to the answer sub-node), not a model property and not an ignore-list entry. `answer` is now scoped to the prose sub-node and `capability.nonAnswerSelectors` names the reasoning/thinking containers plus the user bubble as site-declared non-answer signals. GOAL 163 (2026-09-30, the live re-measurement this file kept asking for): the answer was RE-MEASURED on the deployed build 73fc38e and the narrowed selectors were WRONG — they match ZERO nodes in venice's real DOM, so venice could not have answered. This is the honesty consequence of deriving selectors from a failure instead of from a capture, and it is recorded rather than quietly corrected. Live read of the daemon's own Chrome over CDP (read-only, on the tab the driver had left behind at https://venice.ai/chat/agent/E3nQ9oY) shows the assistant answer IS present and IS 'PONG', inside: DIV.space-y-4 ...prose... > DIV.css-0 > DIV.css-sz3opf > DIV.assistant-content > DIV.assistant. Consequences measured on that live DOM: (a) `[data-message-author-role="assistant"]` does not exist on venice at all (every dataset on the page is empty), and (b) no ANCESTOR of the answer carries a class containing 'message' (the only 'message' class on the page is the unrelated `minds-chat-message-actions` button group), so the old `[class*="message"] [class*="prose"]` could never match either. The distinguishing structural fact is the class TOKEN 'assistant', which is present on the assistant wrapper and absent from the user bubble's wrapper (that one is `assistant-content`, a different token). `[class~="assistant"]` anchors on the token boundary deliberately, so it cannot drift into the user bubble the way a bare `[class*="assistant"]` would. Verified on the live DOM: the new selector matches EXACTLY ONE node, text 'PONG', and excludes both the user bubble ('Reply with exactly: PONG') and the assistant footer ('Worked for < 1s · 1 step · 1 step') that live in the sibling `assistant-content` div. Still requires a re-deploy + a live round trip before venice is called answering; the selector is correct against a real capture, which is strictly more than the previous state, but the PROBE that proves the round trip is still outstanding.
